content.rendered:
Whoever believes in Me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these. Greater. Not smaller. Not the same. Greater. This is what Jesus actually said about the believer’s ministry after His ascension.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, July 17, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Very truly I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.”
John 14:12 (NIV)

Today’s Message

John 14 records Jesus’ farewell discourse to His disciples on the night before the cross. He is preparing them for what will happen when He is no longer physically walking beside them. He has spoken of many mansions in the Father’s house. He has told them He is the way, the truth and the life. And then, halfway through the chapter, He drops a sentence that has quietly reordered the church’s understanding of ministry for two thousand years. Whoever believes in Me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these.

Read that sentence again slowly. Whoever believes. Not the apostles only. Not the specially anointed only. Not the professional clergy only. Whoever believes. That includes you. Will do. Not may do. Will. And the works are not smaller than what Jesus did. They are greater. The Greek word is meizona. It means larger, more significant, of greater extent. The One who healed the sick, cast out demons, raised the dead, calmed the storm and fed the multitudes is telling His followers that their ministry will surpass His in scope.

Two important reasons Jesus gives for this greater-works reality. First, He is going to the Father. His physical presence on earth was limited to one location at a time. His disciples, filled with the Holy Spirit He would send, would be present in every corner of the world simultaneously. The scope of what Christ can accomplish through His body the church is greater than what He could accomplish alone during the incarnation because the church is everywhere at once.

Second, and this is implied throughout the discourse, the greater works flow from the indwelling of the Holy Spirit. Later in the same conversation Jesus will promise the Advocate who will come to the disciples and be with them forever. It is the Spirit-filled believer, connected to the risen Christ, who does the works Jesus did and does greater ones. Not because the believer is greater than Jesus. Because the risen and enthroned Christ is doing greater works through His body than He did during His earthly ministry.

For Gospelbuzz readers, this changes everything about how you approach today. You are not sitting outside the ministry of Jesus watching from a distance. You are inside the greater-works company Jesus called into being on the night before the cross. Whatever He did, you will do. And in ways He specified two thousand years ago, you will do even greater things. Walk in that today. The Spirit who raised Jesus lives in you. The greater works Jesus promised are yours to walk into.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I have been called into the greater-works company of Jesus. Whatever He did, I will do. Not because I am great. Because He is great and He lives in me by the Spirit. The healing He walked in, I walk in. The deliverance He operated in, I operate in. The miracles that followed Him in first-century Galilee, follow me in twenty-first-century daily life. This is not presumption. It is the plain word of Jesus over my life. I walk in that today, confident, expectant, and Spirit-filled. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I have been called into the greater-works company of Jesus. Whatever He did, I will do. The Spirit who raised Him lives in me. I walk in that today.
